## Import and Clean the Land Sales Data
```{python}
# Load data and libraries
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

%pwd
land_sales_df = pd.read_excel('data/MLS_Land_Sales.xlsm')
```

```{python}
def auto_eda(df, target="Sold Price", max_categories=15):
    print(f"\nDataset shape: {df.shape}\n")

    for col in df.columns:
        if col == target:
            continue

        print("="*70)
        print(f"{col}")
        print("-"*70)

        series = df[col]
        missing_pct = series.isna().mean() * 100
        nunique = series.nunique()

        print(f"Missing: {missing_pct:.1f}% | Unique values: {nunique}")

        # ----------------------
        # NUMERIC FEATURES
        # ----------------------
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series):
            print(series.describe())

            if target in df.columns and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[target]):
                corr = df[[col, target]].corr().iloc[0,1]
                print(f"Correlation with {target}: {corr:.3f}")

            # Histogram
            plt.figure()
            series.dropna().hist(bins=40)
            plt.title(f"{col} distribution")
            plt.xlabel(col)
            plt.ylabel("Count")
            plt.show()

            # Boxplot
            plt.figure()
            plt.boxplot(series.dropna(), vert=False)
            plt.title(f"{col} boxplot")
            plt.xlabel(col)
            plt.show()

        # ----------------------
        # CATEGORICAL FEATURES
        # ----------------------
        else:
            if nunique > max_categories:
                print(f"High cardinality — showing top {max_categories} only")

            vc = series.value_counts().head(max_categories)
            print(vc)

            plt.figure()
            vc.plot(kind="bar")
            plt.title(f"{col} (top categories)")
            plt.ylabel("Count")
            plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right")
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.show()
```
## Land Sales Data

### Columns Before the Clean
```{python}
print(list(land_sales_df.columns))
```
```{python}
print(list(land_sales_df.columns))

TARGET = "Sold Price"

# Drops Unwanted Columns
DROP_COLS = [
    # IDs / Keys
    "List Number", "Parcel Number", "Tax Serial #", "Parcel ID Check",
    "St. #", "Address", "Address 2", "Postal Code",

    # Agents / Agencies / PII
    "Agency Name", "Agency Phone", "Agency Email",
    "Listing Agent", "Listing Agent Phone", "Listing Agent Email",
    "Co-Listing Agent",
    "Selling Agency", "Selling Agency Phone", "Selling Agency Email",
    "Selling Agent", "Selling Agent Phone", "Selling Agent Email",
    "Co-Selling Agent", "Owner",

    # URLs / Metadata
    "Photo URL", "mod_timestamp", "Card Format", "Book Section",

    # Directions / Remarks that are mostly noise
    "Directions", "Private Remarks",

    # Post-sale info
    "Sold Date", "Status Change Date", "Withdrawal Date",
    "Cancel Date", "Fallthrough Date", "Concessions Amount", "Concessions4",

    # Too Complicated to deal with at the moment
    "End Date", "Marketing Begin Date", "Lot Dimensions", "Rooms",
    "Features", "Bsmt % Finish", "Public Remarks",

    # Uniform Variables
    "Delayed Marketing Exempt Listing", # N Only
    "State/Province", # Utah Only
    "Status", # C Only
    "Property Type", # Residential Only
]
```
### Columns After the Clean
```{python}
land_sales_clean_df = land_sales_df.drop(columns=[c for c in DROP_COLS if c in land_sales_df.columns])
```
### Univariate EDA
```{python}
auto_eda(land_sales_clean_df, target="Sold Price")
```
### EDA Heatmap
```{python}
num_cols = land_sales_clean_df.select_dtypes(include=np.number)
plt.figure(figsize=(10,8))
plt.imshow(num_cols.corr(), aspect="auto")
plt.colorbar()
plt.xticks(range(len(num_cols.columns)), num_cols.columns, rotation=90)
plt.yticks(range(len(num_cols.columns)), num_cols.columns)
plt.title("Numeric Feature Correlations")
plt.show()
```
### Quick Thoughts
Most of the boolean data is unbalanced a lot of the data is dratically skewed to the right. This makes sense beacause mansions dwarf regular houses. As far as heatmap goes the prices are all highly correlated. Anything with the word sqft is correlated with price. Bedrooms and bathrooms correlat with price. Rooms, bathrooms, and sqft all correlate with each other.
